newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-ZANARDI WINS LONG BEACH INDYCAR WITH PATIENCE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ZANARDI WINS LONG BEACH INDYCAR WITH PATIENCE.

text.p: Italian Allessandro Zanardi, forgoing his usual aggressive style, won the Long Beach Grand Prix CART IndyCar race Sunday with a combination of patience and teamwork.
The 30-year-old Italian took the lead on lap 94 when his teammate, defending champion Jimmy Vasser, had to make a last pit stop for fuel.

In his fourth series win, Zanardi averaged 93.999 mph (151.33 kph) in a Reynard Honda, beating Brazil's Mauricio Gugelmin in a Reynard Mercedes-Benz by 3.82 seconds in the 105-lap race around the 1.59 mile (2.56-km) temporary road circuit.
American Scott Pruett, winner at Surfers Paradise, Australia, last week, finished third in a Reynard Ford.
Zanardi, whose six-race pole-sitting streak ended here on Saturday, had dominated the first two races this year but didn't win due to an accident and a breakdown.
This time, in his second year on the circuit, he did not drive as aggressively and still won. "We didn't dominate but we had the best car today," he said.
"This win was important for us because we had a fast car in Homestead and Surfers but didn't win."
He "The crew did an unbelievable job. They got me way up front on both pit stops. They probably deserve the win more than I do."

Zanardi first took the lead on lap 40, holding it until his second second pit stop on lap 68. That stop turned the lead over to pole winner Gil de Ferran of Brazil. De Ferran's team had trouble fuelling his Reynard Honda, putting him behind Zanardi after he came out of the pits.
Although another Brazilian, Raul Boesel, led from lap 70 to 82, it was because he took his pit stop later than the leaders, due to a different fuel strategy.

Vasser also pitted at a different time from the leaders, due to a puncture after his car was hit from behind early in the race. He too was out of sequence with the leaders and hoped that a yellow flag would allow him to run to the end without stopping for fuel.
"Who'd have thought we'd go 55 laps without a yellow? We just didn't get any breaks today," said the 1996 series champion.
Zanardi was able to cruise to the win.
The fourth race in the 17-race series will take place on April 27 at the one mile (1.6 km) oval at Nazareth, Pennsylvania.
